name: FlashDecoding++: Faster Large Language Model Inference on GPUs
problem: Attention at decode time is memory-bandwidth-bound on the KV cache, and flat GEMMs of differing shapes hit different hardware bottlenecks - so a single schedule cannot be optimal across batch size, head count and context length, and doubles the cost of KV reads (the 'read amplification' of naive flash-decode splitting).
mechanism: A decode-optimised attention kernel: parallelise over KV length, head and batch with a per-workload split heuristic; keep Q in registers/SRAM across the KV loop to eliminate read amplification; use different GEMV vs GEMM templates with tensor-core and adaptive pipeline scheduling; double buffering; and a heuristic dataflow that adapts to the hardware resource bottleneck given the input shape.
speedup_reported: Paper's own claims (abstract): up to 4.86x on NVIDIA GPUs and 2.18x on AMD GPUs vs HuggingFace implementations, and an average 1.37x vs state-of-the-art LLM inference engines on mainstream LLMs. Both baselines named (HF implementations; unnamed SOTA engines - the weaker of the two comparisons).
notes: arXiv ID 2311.01282 verified via abs-page meta tags on 2026-10-03; title matches.
